messages:
maria.gomez: Heads-up — CI flagged a regression in the audit-event conformance check right after the KMS envelope format switch (kms_v2). failing test: 'audit_event_schema_checker::validate_envelope'. @samir.patel can you triage?

audit-bot: [CI] Workflow 'schema-conformance' failed on commit 8f3d2b. Tests failed: 1 assertion. Logs: https://ci.internal/runs/12345 :warning:

samir.patel: looking now. quick skim of the failing assertion shows an unexpected top-level key 'encryption_metadata' with nested 'kms_key_id' as string vs the expected object. might be a schema drift.

kevin.liu: we landed the kms_v2 change in runtime last night — it wrapped the envelope metadata to be more compact. did we update the conformance reference-set?

maria.gomez: i thought the conformance reference-set was supposed to be backward-compatible. if runtime emits the new compact envelope we should still validate. either the schema needs to accept the compact form, or the checker needs to accept both.

samir.patel: reproducing locally with the sample payload from the failing CI run. paste of minimal repro below:

```
{
  "event_type": "user.auth",
  "timestamp": "2025-11-03T18:22:11Z",
  "envelope": {
    "payload_ref": "s3://audit/2025/11/03/evt.json",
    "encryption_metadata": "kms_v2:arn:aws:kms:..."
  }
}
```

samir.patel: our schema currently expects encryption_metadata to be an object: {"kms": {"key_id": "...", "ctx": {...}}}. the runtime now emits a compact string when KMS returns a wrapped token.

kevin.liu: oof. we toggled compact mode to reduce token size for the stream pipeline. i can revert quickly if that's the fastest fix for customer-facing audit events.

maria.gomez: For short-term mitigation: can the schema-checker accept a string or object for encryption_metadata? that preserves compatibility and keeps runtime change in place. longer-term we should standardize the envelope contract.

oncall-sre: FYI — this regression causes a customer-facing audit validation failure in Dedicated tenants using strict schema gating. Seeing two customers with automated ingestion fail on the new payload.

samir.patel: i can patch the checker to accept the compact string format and add a warning-level linting message when string form is seen. will also add a convertor helper that expands the compact token into the object used by our postprocessing.

kevin.liu: can we get a quick unit test added to the conformance-reference-set to cover both forms? i want to avoid CI flakes later.

maria.gomez: yes — add tests for: (1) legacy object form, (2) compact string form, (3) malformed string -> should fail. also add a note in the CHANGELOG about the envelope acceptance behavior.

samir.patel: creating a PR with the checker patch + tests now. link when ready.

audit-bot: [CI] New PR #5123 opened by samir.patel: 'schema: accept compact kms_v2 envelope string for encryption_metadata' — tests added.

samir.patel: PR: https://git.internal/r/5123 — pinging @maria.gomez for review. aiming to merge within the hour and re-run the failing workflow.

maria.gomez: reviewing now. leaving inline nit comments but LGTM on the approach. agree with warning-level lint for now.

oncall-sre: once merged, please backport to the dedicated-ops branch and trigger a canary for the affected customers. i'll coordinate the rollback plan if anything else breaks.

kevin.liu: follow-up: i'll add an integration smokecheck that runs the new compact payload through the ingress pipeline to ensure no downstream consumers choke on the string form.

maria.gomez: thank you all. after merge let's schedule a short RFC to lock the envelope contract (schema vs runtime encoding) so this doesn't recur.

samir.patel: merged and re-run kicked off. CI now shows green on the previously failing job. closing the thread after canary verification. :tada:
